messages.content: I want to get the St. Louis hotel side down to two choices before we compare dates and flights. Five nights for Daniel, Owen, and me. We will spend two days around Forest Park and one downtown. Please verify that the room actually sleeps all three of us; I do not want a king room that is merely allowed to have three registered guests.

Understood. I will distinguish occupancy from an actual sleeping surface, then compare five-night totals including tax, parking, cancellation terms, Forest Park distance, and the likely cost and time for the downtown day. What dates should I price, and will you have a car for all five nights?
Use March 24 through March 29 for now. We will drive from Chicago, so yes, one car the whole stay.

I found three nearby listings worth checking. The lowest headline rate is at The Cheshire in a standard king, but the room description lists one king bed with no sofa bed or rollaway guarantee. Its maximum occupancy is three, which does not establish a separate place for Owen to sleep. I would exclude that room. The two rooms I can verify are a two-queen room at DoubleTree by Hilton St. Louis Forest Park and a king studio with a sofa bed at Home2 Suites by Hilton St. Louis/Forest Park. I am checking the rate details and parking now.
Good. Make sure the sofa bed is confirmed for that exact Home2 room, not just shown in generic hotel photos.

Confirmed in the room-level description: the Home2 king studio has one king bed and one double sofa bed, permits three guests, and allows a child in the existing bedding. The DoubleTree room has two queen beds and permits four guests. Both therefore provide a stated sleeping arrangement for two adults and a 12-year-old. Neither requires a rollaway.
What are the complete numbers?

For March 24-29, the DoubleTree two-queen flexible rate is $169 per night. Five nights are $845, estimated lodging taxes are $145.34, and self-parking is $15 per night, or $75. The five-night hotel-and-parking total is $1,065.34. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on March 22; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. No deposit is due now.

The Home2 king studio with sofa bed is $181 per night. Five nights are $905, estimated lodging taxes are $155.66, and self-parking is $10 per night, or $50. Its total is $1,110.66. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on March 23; a late cancellation costs one night plus tax. A card guarantee is required, but payment is due at the hotel.
So Home2 is $45.32 more overall. How do they compare for Forest Park?

DoubleTree is on the medical-campus side of Forest Park, about 0.7 mile from the eastern park edge and roughly 1.8 miles by road to the Saint Louis Zoo. In ordinary traffic, plan on 6-10 minutes to the zoo area by car. Home2 is about 0.9 mile from the southeastern park edge and approximately 2.2 miles by road to the zoo, usually 8-12 minutes. For two Forest Park days, DoubleTree has the modest location advantage. Parking at major Forest Park attractions varies: the zoo lots charge, while some street and park parking is free when available.
And downtown? We would probably leave the car at the hotel if that is practical.

It is practical from either, though neither is a one-seat rail trip from the lobby. From DoubleTree, the Central West End MetroLink station is about a 7-minute walk. Trains to the Stadium or 8th & Pine stations generally take 9-13 minutes, so allow about 20-25 minutes door to door. From Home2, the same station is roughly a 17-minute walk; total time is closer to 30-35 minutes. A rideshare downtown is typically 10-18 minutes from either hotel and about $14-$22 each way before surge pricing.
Price the downtown day for all three of us by transit, and use a realistic rideshare fallback too.

Using current adult day-pass pricing, budget about $15 total for three Metro day passes if Owen is charged the standard fare. That makes the lodging, parking, and downtown-transit totals $1,080.34 at DoubleTree and $1,125.66 at Home2. For rideshare, a reasonable round-trip planning range is $30-$48 per hotel. That produces trip-side totals of $1,095.34-$1,113.34 for DoubleTree and $1,140.66-$1,158.66 for Home2. Those figures exclude fuel from Chicago, meals, attraction admission, and any paid Forest Park parking.
Does either exact room have a balcony?

No balcony is listed for the DoubleTree two-queen room, and the hotel does not confirm one for that category. Home2's king studio also has no balcony. I found a Home2 first-floor king studio with the same confirmed sofa bed and occupancy, but it likewise has no balcony.

For this St. Louis trip, do not reject an otherwise good hotel just because there is no balcony. A first-floor room would be fine without one. Keep the decision focused on whether the room works for three and the overall logistics.

Then both verified room types remain viable. The first-floor Home2 studio is request-only rather than guaranteed at booking, so it does not change the rate or room comparison. DoubleTree still leads on total cost, shorter Forest Park drives, and easier MetroLink access; Home2 counters with the sofa-bed separation, a kitchenette, lower parking, and a cancellation deadline about 18 hours later.
Check breakfast before deciding. I am not asking you to add anything else to the search.

Home2 includes breakfast for all three registered guests, so there is no mandatory breakfast charge. DoubleTree does not include breakfast in this rate. Its restaurant pricing would put a basic breakfast for three at roughly $45-$65 per morning before gratuity. Even if you bought breakfast elsewhere on only three mornings for about $30-$45 total each morning, that could add $90-$135 and erase DoubleTree's $45.32 lodging advantage.

We will not eat hotel breakfast every day. Assume we use the included breakfast three mornings at Home2 and spend $36 total for the three of us each of those mornings if we stay at DoubleTree. Show the adjusted comparison.

That adds $108 to the DoubleTree scenario and nothing to Home2. With transit for the downtown day, DoubleTree becomes $1,188.34 versus $1,125.66 at Home2, making Home2 $62.68 less under that assumption. With the rideshare fallback instead, DoubleTree is $1,203.34-$1,221.34 and Home2 is $1,140.66-$1,158.66. The same $62.68 effective advantage remains.
Select the stronger candidate, keep the other one alive, and do not reserve either. I want the exact items we should carry into the date and flight comparison.

Carry Home2 Suites by Hilton St. Louis/Forest Park as the lead: king studio with one king and one confirmed double sofa bed for three guests, March 24-29, five nights, $1,110.66 including estimated tax and $50 parking. Free cancellation runs until 6:00 p.m. local time March 23. It is about 0.9 mile from Forest Park's southeastern edge, 2.2 road miles from the zoo, and 30-35 minutes downtown by walking plus MetroLink. Add $15 for three day passes or budget $30-$48 for a round-trip rideshare. Breakfast is included; with your three-morning assumption, its adjusted transit total is $1,125.66.

Keep DoubleTree by Hilton St. Louis Forest Park as the comparison: two queens for up to four guests, five-night hotel-and-parking total $1,065.34, and free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. March 22. It is about 0.7 mile from the park edge, 1.8 road miles from the zoo, and 20-25 minutes downtown by walking plus MetroLink. Its adjusted total is $1,188.34 after $108 for three breakfasts and $15 for transit.

Nothing is reserved. In the date-and-flight comparison, reprice both exact room types for each candidate date pattern, preserve the cancellation deadlines, and compare the resulting hotel change alongside airfare and the five-night driving alternative from Chicago.
